GTA 6 Play Tips — mechanics, numbers, traps

30 mechanical tips with the actual systems and figures behind them — no filler. Each one is sourced.

Scan every car with WAiNK before you steal itBefore you touch a parked car, hold Up on the D-pad, open WAiNK and hold R1/RB on the vehicle. The scan shows its security (locked, alarmed, keyless), its tracker tier, its sale value and exactly what registration would cost — everything you need to decide whether it is worth stealing at all. Know the three tracker tiers before you commitTrackers decide a stolen car's fate. No tracker: Moses will buy it or register it from Chapter 2. Standard tracker: nobody can modify or register it until Pay 'n' Spray registration opens in Chapter 3. Advanced tracker: it actively reports your position to police at low speed, and only Randy's trade (and, per gta.guide, Pay 'n' Spray after a later Randy job) deals in them. Keep your speed up in an advanced-tracker carAn advanced tracker transmits your location to the police whenever you drive slowly or sit still — a red icon above the minimap fills as your speed drops. Keep your speed up for the whole run; as you near Randy's garage the icon greys out and the signal dies. This is the whole mechanic of the Zorrusso delivery. Spend the free first registration on the best car, not the first carMoses waives the registration fee exactly once, and later registrations cost $1,400 to $40,650 depending on the car (the hands-on WAiNK scan range reported by Space4Games). So decline whatever you drove in with if it is ordinary: the free slot belongs on the most valuable tracker-free car you can find and actually want to keep, because that car becomes Lucia's first personal vehicle. Respray first — registration is refused without itRegistration is a two-step order and the order matters: Moses will only register a car after it has been resprayed. Talk to him, choose Respray and change the colour, then choose Register. Arriving in a car you refuse to repaint means no registration. Work around Moses' sales cooldownAfter each sale Moses' garage shuts briefly. PowerPyx and GTABase put the wait at roughly two real-time minutes, and the practical rhythm is to steal the next car during the cooldown so he is open when you return. Be aware gta6.house and Game Rant instead describe a few in-game hours between sales and a daily sales limit — either way, car-flipping is steady money, not fast money. Never steal a sale car near Moses' shopMoses turns away cars stolen too close to his own shop — he will not fence his neighbours' cars. Take sale cars from the main road through central Port Gellhorn instead, and lose any wanted level before you drive in: fences will not deal while police are looking for you. No free garage slot, no registrationEvery registration consumes a garage slot, and your vehicle roster starts at just three slots. Purchasable garages add only one slot each regardless of price, while the free story garages are the generous ones — Thompson Court holds two and Pegassi Residences holds three. If registration is refused, a full roster is the first thing to check. Parking a stolen car is not registering itLeaving a stolen car in your garage only parks it. Registration is the separate act that makes it a personal vehicle: permanently yours, stored against loss and callable to your position through the Scooter Bros app. An unregistered car you abandon is just a car you abandoned. Bank $5,000 into Family Savings before Tourist TrapStarting Tourist Trap wipes Jason's pocket cash, his BuckMe checking balance, the floorboard stash, the house and every personal vehicle. The one exception is Family Savings: fill it to its $5,000 Chapter 1 cap (which also completes the Buckin' Broke goal and raises your checking limit to $15,000), then convert what's left into guns, clothes and tattoos, which all survive. The $5,000 Rainy Day Fund lockbox also survives the fire and can be collected later. Remember the account is one-way: deposits can never be withdrawn, and in Chapter 2 savings do not count toward spendable-cash goals like the $15,000 Vice City fund. Deposit pocket cash — it dies with youPocket cash is the fragile form of money: it is lost when you are wasted or busted, and GTABase puts the carrying limit at $20,000. Deposit at an ATM into BuckMe checking whenever the total climbs, and note PowerPyx's observation that purchases can be deducted digitally even at zero pocket cash — there is little reason to walk around loaded. Crack the crab outpost in Chapter 2, not Chapter 1The Pelican Valley crab research outpost is a three-code, one-time puzzle: the floorboard word CLEAVES opens the computer (one guide, Space4Games, argues the real password is SOFTSH3LL — try CLEAVES first, as four other guides agree), the safe code is 0072 (double the successful specimen, 0036), and the boathouse keypad is 0212. It pays about $1,000 cash, $10,000 in marked bills and the unique Crabshack VF5 SMG — and because Chapter 1 wipes your cash, running it in Chapter 2 is strictly better. Marked bills need a fence — and Yasmani pays bestMarked bills are not money until a fence launders them. Dunk in Port Gellhorn takes them from Chapter 2 (after Slam Dunk) but pays very low rates; Yasmani in Little Cuba pays high rates once Chapter 3 opens. If the bag can wait, it is worth waiting — and from Credit Check in Chapter 3, the Dye Pack Jammer lets you handle marked bills without the packs bursting. Do Credit Check early — it unlocks the robbery economyRaul's Credit Check mission pays $6,000, hands you the Dye Pack Jammer, and is the gate for the robbery economy: 14 small banks paying $5,000–$45,000 and 7 payday loan stores paying $2,000–$25,000 only open after it. Push to Credit Check early in Chapter 3 if money is your problem. Climb the payout ladder instead of selling to the first fenceCar income climbs a ladder as the story opens fences: about $1,000 per untracked car at Moses in Chapter 2, typically ~$2,500+, up to $4,000+ for a good standard-tracker car in perfect condition at Pay 'n' Spray in Chapter 3, $30,000 or more per perfect-condition supercar on Randy's Wish List from mid-Chapter 3, and up to $205,000 per bank vault at the end of Chapter 4. Sell each car to the best buyer its tracker allows, not the nearest one. Deliver Yasmani's first piece immediately to earn the Snap GunDeliver Yasmani's first requested piece the moment you have it. ShowGamer, ScreenRant and Sportskeeda all report he hands over the Snap Gun at that first delivery, so you get the silent lockpick for the remaining two jewelry jobs instead of forcing their back doors. Note the tool only opens the door — the building's alarm system still has to be disarmed separately. A vault robbery is an instant four stars — plan the exit firstA large vault run is mechanical: follow a security van until it stops at a bank, walk in behind the guard while the vault stands open, and take the marked bills. Expect an instant four-star wanted level the moment you enter — the payout (up to $205,000) is priced for the escape, so plan the getaway before you go in, not after. Run the numbers before buying Scooter Bros' $12,000 passScooter Bros delivery costs $100 per call, or a one-time $12,000 for three free deliveries a day. The maths only favours the pass if you would otherwise pay for roughly 120 deliveries — buy it late, once you are constantly swapping cars, not in Chapter 2 when cash is tight and one registered car does everything. Find the pink zone and hold it — that's every lockpick in the gameThe Slim Jim and the Key Cloner share one minigame: work the right stick until the indicator turns from white to pink, then hold it there until the bar fills. Rushing the stick just restarts your progress on the lock. The same pink-zone hold is how you clone a key at a keyless car's door in Chapter 3. Don't break into a keyless car before Chapter 3Before the Key Cloner, a keyless car is a trap: you can smash your way in, set off the alarm, and still not be able to drive it away. Scan first — if WAiNK shows keyless security, walk away until Randy gives you the cloner in Chapter 3. Once installed (Settings, key_cloner_v1.6.9) it covers both Jason and Lucia permanently and skips the hotwire minigame entirely. Your car is your arsenal — you only carry four gunsYou carry at most four guns on foot: two sidearms and two long guns, one slung and one in hand, and no upgrade ever raises that cap. Everything else lives in your personal vehicle's trunk, and trunk capacity varies by vehicle — some hold two stash bags, others six. Choose your ride before a job the way you'd choose a loadout, because your car is your arsenal. Bought guns come back; found guns don'tA gun you bought at Ammu-Nation is yours forever: lose it and you can recover it from a weapon locker or your car's trunk. A gun you picked up — including the shotgun, carbine and armor in police car trunks — is gone permanently once lost. Treat found guns as expendable and spend money only on the weapons you plan to rely on. Sell your cards — your collection progress is permanentSelling a collectible card never removes it from your Collections registry — sets complete and trophies count whether or not you still hold the physical card. So sell freely: commons go for about $20, rare cards for $1,000 or more, and duplicates are pure cash. For 100% you need 15 of the 18 sets (372 cards minimum), not all 480. Standouts are one-of-a-kind — verify the name on screenStandout vehicles are one-off, pre-styled versions of normal vehicles parked in fixed spots — 280 of them by the in-game Progress database count (database pin counts of found standouts vary — GTABase lists 254 so far, while Dexerto's map claims 283 spawns, likely counting edition and GTA+ vehicles differently). 'Discovering' one means walking up to it, and GTA6Info's advice is to check that the standout's name actually appears on screen before counting it, because a regular version of the same model parked nearby looks almost identical. The Girlypop set is an endgame hunt, not an early oneFinding all 16 Girlypop standout vehicles unlocks the Neon Jungle screen-filter cheat. Two catches: as of the latest guides only 14 of the 16 have been publicly named and located, and like every GTA 6 cheat it only becomes usable after you have finished the story — so the hunt is an endgame project, not an early one. Heat is per-identifier — change what they actually sawLosing the stars is not the end: police keep heat icons for everything they know — your appearance, clothing, vehicle, weapon, CCTV footage and whether your partner was with you — and each icon clears separately. A haircut does nothing if they know your outfit. Change the specific things they identified, swap vehicles, and splitting up from your partner drops a level outright. Hollow stars are your free exit — walk, don't runStar appearance tells you what police know. Hollow/transparent stars mean a crime was reported but the suspect is unknown — leave the area calmly before officers arrive and you may never be pursued at all. Solid white means identified and in pursuit; flashing means they have lost sight of you; red means the chase is over but the area stays hot with your description. Learn the fixed keypad codes — but robbery safes randomiseStory and puzzle keypads use fixed codes worth memorising: 092319 opens the Key Lento party house garage (Spiderweb Coquette inside), 2727 opens the '74 Vamos garage, and 92665 opens the Del Rio Boulevard garage with Vanessa's Growler and a free garage to keep. But open-world robbery safes randomise their combinations per save — if a listed code fails somewhere else, the real one is written down on site. Keep rotating manual saves — there is no mission replayGTA 6 has no mission replay and no gold medals to chase. The only way back to a chapter-exclusive moment is a manual save you made yourself, so keep rotating saves at the start and end of every chapter — and specifically before Tourist Trap, Checking Out and the finale sequence. Hourglass markers outrank everything else on your mapOptional missions marked with an hourglass expire as the story advances. The named traps are Shirley's errands and the balcony meditation in Chapter 1, Race Against Yago in Chapter 3, and This Is a Free Call From… in Chapter 4. The identified missables are not required for 100% or the Platinum, but an hourglass marker should always outrank whatever you were doing.
